---
title: "Confidence moves the tails, not the middle"
subtitle: "Catalog C-03 (with C-04)"
description: "Table 2 of the paper, live: the same target mean with four levels of confidence gives four Gamma priors whose majority dominance barely moves while extreme dominance and the mass near zero change a lot."
toc: false
---

The elicited mean is the same in every row, "about 5 clusters among 100 units". Only the
confidence changes, through the variance inflation factor: sigma^2 = VIF (mu_K − 1), so
VIF 1.25, 1.5, 2.5 and 5 ask for a variance of 5, 6, 10 and 20.

```{=html}
<div id="w-vif" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/vif-sensitivity.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxVif = DPX["vif-sensitivity"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-vif"), {});
</script>
```

- **The prior on alpha widens.** From VIF 1.25 to 5 the calibrated prior goes from
  Gamma(7.13, 7.41) to Gamma(0.62, 0.56): its mean stays near 1 (0.96 to 1.11) but its spread
  grows.
- **The mean drives majority dominance.** Pr(W_SB > .5) moves only from .53 to .61.
- **The variance drives extreme dominance and collapse.** Pr(W_SB > .9) moves from .15 to .36,
  and the mass near zero, Pr(alpha < .1), from 0 to .18: a low-confidence count target quietly
  allows one cluster to take almost everything.
- The two-lenses panels (C-04) show the same prior as a count distribution and as a weight
  distribution; J changes only the count.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Every row is solved in the browser by TSMM (dp-core `tsmmFit`) and matches the paper's
Table 2 and OSM Table F.4 (checked against DPprior 2.0.0 on [the parity page](tsmm-parity.qmd)).
The lens panels are the widget of [One alpha, two lenses](../bridge/two-lenses.qmd), reused
unchanged.
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
**In DPprior Studio.** For a whole grid of target means and confidence levels at once, use the Sensitivity panel of [DPprior Studio](https://joonho.shinyapps.io/dpprior-studio/), the Shiny app that
accompanies the package (built on DPprior 1.1.0; it may take a moment to wake up). This site does
not rebuild what Studio already does.
:::

(for example `?preset=5`).
